terms.gloss: a line, a file of people
evidence: Traupman 102: longum agmen facere, to form a long line
terms.comment: Classically agmen is “a collected multitude in motion” (Lewis & Short), a column on the march; Traupman uses it for a line of people. Its use for a queue standing still is his, and the phrase is not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

sources: Lewis & Short: agmen
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 102.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
